snippet.title: Bunkers: The Cold War Plan for Surviving Atomic Destruction | Full Documentary
snippet.description:
For decades, humanity lived under the constant threat of nuclear annihilation. Hidden beneath forests, mountains, and cities across Europe, vast underground bunkers were built to survive the outbreak of World War III. From Soviet missile silos concealed deep inside Lithuania to secret West German civil defense command centers and East Germany’s heavily fortified communications hubs, governments prepared for the moment nuclear war would erupt between NATO and the Warsaw Pact. Massive concrete walls, anti-radiation systems, sealed airlocks, and underground control rooms formed part of a terrifying strategy based on Mutually Assured Destruction during the Cold War.

The documentary also uncovers Albania’s extraordinary bunker obsession under communist dictator Enver Hoxha, who transformed the isolated Balkan nation into one of the most heavily fortified countries on Earth with hundreds of thousands of bunkers scattered across the landscape. Through rare archival footage, former military personnel, Cold War maps, and access to once top-secret facilities, the film reveals how fear of nuclear war shaped entire societies and created underground worlds built for the end of civilization itself.

snippet.title: The Real Reason Morocco’s Jews Left

From thriving mellahs and rich traditions to secret escape routes and Mossad rescue missions, the story of Moroccan Jews is one of resilience, identity, and exile. snippet.title: Strike on Iran: The Nuclear Question (updated documentary) | FRONTLINE (PBS)
snippet.description:
An investigation into the status of Iran’s nuclear program amid the second round of U.S.-Israeli military action in less than a year. (March 2026 update)

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

In the weeks since the U.S. and Israel began bombarding Iran, President Trump has repeatedly justified the strikes by claiming Iran had posed an imminent nuclear threat. But nine months earlier, in the wake of U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran in June 2025, the message coming from Washington was that Iran’s key nuclear facilities had been “obliterated.”

Drawing on new reporting, satellite imagery analysis and interviews, this investigation is an updated presentation of our December 2025 documentary by the same name.

In September of last year, directors Adam Desiderio and Sebastian Walker, who is also the film’s correspondent, visited sites hit in the June 2025 U.S.-Israeli strikes and sat down with one of Iran’s most powerful officials, Ali Larijani — in what turned out to be the last on-camera interview he gave to an American news outlet before his assassination earlier this month in an Israeli airstrike. 

Since the current war began, the team has been talking to experts and officials and analyzing satellite imagery with The Washington Post, Bellingcat and Evident Media to try to understand the truth about what remains of Iran’s nuclear program.

Their findings offer valuable insights into a continuing conflict that has rippled across the Middle East, killing thousands — including children at an elementary school — and displacing millions.

“Strike on Iran” is a FRONTLINE production with Mongoose Pictures in association with The ‪@WashingtonPost‬ ‪@evidentmedia‬ and ‪@bellingcatofficial‬. It is written, produced and directed by Adam Desiderio and Sebastian Walker. The correspondent is Sebastian Walker. The reporters are Nilo Tabrizy, Jarrett Ley, Souad Mekhennet, Trevor Ball, Carlos Gonzales and Sebastian Vandermeersch. The senior producers are Dan Edge and Eamonn Matthews. The editor-in-chief and executive producer of FRONTLINE is Raney Aronson-Rath.

snippet.title: Animal River Challenge: Eye of the Eagle
snippet.description:
Venture deep into the South American rainforest and witness the extraordinary lives of its iconic giants: harpy eagles, tapirs, anacondas, and more await you!

Join wildlife filmmakers Reiner Bergemans and Young Sandy as they embark on a decade-long quest to uncover the secrets of Guyana’s Esakibo River ecosystem. Experience the lush biodiversity of the untouched rainforest, from elusive tapirs and giant otters to the spectacular harpy eagle—nature’s most powerful raptor, capable of preying on sloths and monkeys high in the canopy. The video reveals rare footage of jungle drama, harpy eagle nesting, epic river journeys over dangerous rapids and waterfalls, and fascinating animal behaviors shaped by fierce competition for territory.

You’ll get an up-close look at the layered world of the rainforest: capuchin monkeys showing tool-use intelligence, giant armadillos burrowing for insects, caiman lurking in quiet pools, and vibrant birdlife such as scarlet macaws and toucans. The expedition faces daunting challenges, from climbing towering capoque trees for a bird’s-eye view to braving torrential downpours before filming an elusive harpy chick’s hatching. The film also explores survival strategies—how predators hunt, how herbivores adapt, and the critical role each species plays in this fragile web of life.

Perfect for anyone curious about South American wildlife, rainforest ecosystems, or the secrets of one of Earth’s richest habitats, this video brings the wonders and struggles of the Amazon right to your screen.

snippet.title: Richard Hammond's Wild Weather: Wind: The Invisible Force
snippet.description:
Witness the true power of wind—the invisible force behind Earth’s wildest weather, from fire whirls to tornadoes, and discover secrets of extreme weather phenomena!

Explore how wind shapes our world, drives extreme storms, and forms spectacular spinning weather like tornadoes and fire whirls. Journey from Mount Washington, home of record-breaking winds, to the bushfire-prone forests of Australia, where flaming vortices spin to life. Through daring experiments and hands-on demonstrations, learn how atmospheric pressure, terrain, and temperature create the most unpredictable and deadly weather events.

Dive inside a whirlwind of science as we build a fire tornado, explain the basics of wind formation, and reveal why tornado spin speeds near the ground remain one of meteorology’s greatest mysteries. Meet pioneering researchers tackling these challenges with groundbreaking technology—from advanced wind tunnels in Canada to armored storm-chasing vehicles in Tornado Alley. Experience the adrenaline of launching probes into a live twister, and learn why uncovering these secrets could save lives.

Whether you’re fascinated by storm science, extreme weather systems, or just want to know how to read the skies, this video gives you a front-row seat to weather like you’ve never seen before.

snippet.title: Holy Wars: In the Name of Allah
snippet.description:
Discover the epic saga of Islam in the Middle Ages—its rise, triumphs, and turbulent encounters with war, science, and coexistence. Explore how religion and power shaped history.

Dive into a vivid historical journey tracing the development of Islamic civilization from its humble beginnings in Mecca to becoming a global force that transformed the medieval world. This video examines the paradox of faith and violence—how Islam, synonymous with "peace," contributed to both groundbreaking cultural advancements and fierce conflicts, including its encounters with crusaders, Mongols, and internal divisions between Sunnis and Shiites. You'll learn how Islamic empires fostered scientific innovation, preserved Greek philosophy, and influenced Europe, especially through centers like Baghdad and Cordoba.

Key moments covered include the fall of Baghdad to the Mongols, the legendary battle of Ain Jalut, the emergence of military slave dynasties, and the coexistence (and rivalry) between Christians, Jews, and Muslims in Spain. The story reveals how Arabic poetry, navigation, medicine, and even the game of chess made their mark on Western civilization. The video also confronts the darker legacies—like the origins of terrorism with the Assassins—clarifying that violence and terror in the name of Islam are historical aberrations and abuses, not reflections of its core teachings. Packed with insights, this documentary is your guide to understanding the enduring impact and complex heritage of Islam in the medieval era.

snippet.title: Targeting Albert Speer: The Jealousy and Intrigue Inside Hitler’s Regime
snippet.description:
By 1942, Nazi Germany was losing the war it had started. snippet.title: Great Moments In Evolution: The Journey From One Cell To Humanity
snippet.description:
How did life rise from a single cell to the astonishing diversity of animals, plants and humans on Earth today? This extra long evolution documentary follows the greatest turning points in natural history, beginning around four billion years ago, when life first emerged in the ancient oceans. One angle explores LUCA, Darwin, the Cambrian explosion, eyesight, intelligence, animal communication, sleep and Tiktaalik, the creature that helped open the path from water to land.

A second angle reveals how life survived catastrophe. Around 250 million years ago, Earth suffered its greatest mass extinction, wiping out more than 90 percent of ocean species and almost as many on land. Yet evolution continued, creating new predators, dinosaurs, eggs, sex, migration and the rise of mammals. From feathered dinosaurs and emperor penguins to CRISPR, mammoths and the threat of a sixth extinction, this documentary tells the ultimate story of survival, adaptation and life’s greatest inventions.

snippet.title: Brown Gold Rush: Inside Madagascar's Violent Vanilla Trade | Full Documentary
snippet.description:
It is the second most expensive spice in the world, found in almost every kitchen in Europe, and it is tearing apart one of the poorest countries on earth. Madagascar supplies 80% of the global vanilla harvest, but while the price of a single kilogram soared from €35 to over €600 in just a few years, 92% of the island's population still lives on less than two euros a day. Behind the familiar scent of childhood and Christmas baking lies a world of violence, theft, corruption, and death. Farmers sleep in their fields to guard their crops. Lynch mobs patrol at night with machetes. A radio journalist has been kidnapped and threatened with death for simply reporting the truth. And somewhere in the chain between a Madagascan jungle and a supermarket yogurt, the question of who actually profits from the brown gold remains very difficult to answer.

snippet.title: Holy Wars: Christians against Christians
snippet.description:
Discover how Europe’s greatest wars over religion reshaped not only the continent but the very idea of the modern state. Explore the faith, violence, and transformation at the heart of history.

This gripping documentary delves into the turbulent centuries when religion and power collided, unleashing devastating wars like the Reformation conflicts and the Thirty Years’ War. How did Christianity—preaching peace—become entangled in bloodshed? Follow the rise of Martin Luther, the explosive spread of Protestantism through the printing press, and the descent into fanaticism and revolution. From the brutal Peasants’ War to the carnage of Magdeburg, witness how mercenary armies, political intrigue, and relentless violence scarred a continent.

But out of the ashes emerged the foundation for modern Europe: the separation of church and state, the rise of powerful nation-states, and the concept of civil law above religious strife. Learn how thinkers like Hobbes reimagined authority, how Prussia became a beacon of religious tolerance, and how the lessons of these conflicts echo in today’s pursuit of peace and justice. If you’re fascinated by the intersection of religion, history, and politics—or searching for the roots of today’s Europe—this is essential viewing.

snippet.title: Secrets of the Magna Carta: S01 EP01
snippet.description:
Discover the dramatic, world-changing story of Magna Carta—history’s most valuable document and its fight to secure freedom and justice for all.

Journey from the turbulent reign of King John to the forging of the Magna Carta on the banks of the River Thames in 1215—a turning point that challenged tyranny, birthed the roots of democracy, and enshrined rights that echo in today’s struggles for liberty. This documentary reveals how the Great Charter didn't just shape English law; it revolutionized property rights, taxation, and the relationship between people and power, paving the way for future revolts and the rise of parliament. 

Explore how legends like Robin Hood were entwined with real tax revolts, how feudal peasants struggled under harsh lords, and how the rights promised in Magna Carta trickled down from barons and bishops to guilds, peasants, and eventually ordinary citizens. Follow the Charter’s legacy through guild monopolies, the Peasants’ Revolt, the birth of free markets and liberties, and even across the Atlantic to inspire America’s founding ideals. Through centuries of rebellion, innovation, and debate, see how Magna Carta remains a living challenge to unchecked authority, reminding us never to take hard-won freedoms for granted.
